stances.claim: CPAs, CFOs and CEOs become 'purveyors of liberty and prosperity under the rule of law' whenever their reports and actions embody TATS (Transparency, Accountability, Truth, Sustainability). The four TATS values are not merely professional standards but the mechanism by which the accounting profession actively advances liberty and prosperity for society.
stances.rhetorical_move: professional-elevation argument: transforms accountants from number-processors into civic agents of liberty and prosperity through the TATS framework
stances.confidence: asserted as CJP's keynote thesis for the PICPA induction

stances.claim: 'Truth is eternal and limitless; truth is not bound by sovereignty, or territory, or ideology, or legality.' What is true in America is also true in the Philippines, in Asia and in the world: the best way to conquer poverty and create prosperity is to unleash the entrepreneurial genius of people. MLK is quoted not because of his nationality but because of the truth he said simply and profoundly.
stances.rhetorical_move: universality-of-truth argument: displaces the American origin of the MLK quote by asserting that truth transcends sovereignty

stances.claim: Different nations start their development journey in different ways -- some with economic improvement first (China), some with political liberty first (US), some with both simultaneously -- but all nations 'eventually and inevitably need and deserve liberty and prosperity in equal measure.' There is no permanent trade-off, only different sequencing.
stances.rhetorical_move: sequencing-not-substitution argument: acknowledges the China/authoritarian-development model while insisting on ultimate convergence to full liberty and prosperity

notable_anecdotes: Dolly Miguel's P50M+ audit fee defense: Dolly's expertise in overcoming 'intense grilling by members of the Audit Committees' while proving that fees 'sometimes in excess of P50 million annually from just one of the companies' are reasonable and fair because of 'hard work, integrity, independence, accuracy and on-time submission.'

PLDT's multi-jurisdiction audit: as the only Philippine company listed on the NYSE and effectively controlled by Hong Kong-listed First Pacific, PLDT's audit requires compliance with US federal law, US SEC, New York state/city laws, NYSE rules, HK laws, HKSE rules, Philippine laws, SEC, and PSE rules -- 'a reasonable familiarity of these foreign laws and rules' as the baseline.

Washington SyCip as original FLP trustee: the SGV founder 'did not only join and lend his name to the Foundation. He also contributed a substantial sum.' After his death, Amando Tetangco Jr. agreed to take his place.

CJP's self-deprecation as a non-CPA: 'I do not know what kind of funny wind struck President Dolly that impelled her to invite me to be your inducting officer and guest speaker today. Unlike all of you, I am not a certified public accountant, not even a commerce or business administration graduate. I am just a humble lawyer from a mass-based private university.'

The North Korea / South Korea contrast: rising from the ruins of the same war, one (South Korea) relied on entrepreneurship, private initiative, innovation, creativity, freedom and hard work; the other (North Korea) 'wallows in abject poverty as a result of its tight grip on creativity and inordinate fear of entrepreneurship, education, freedom and prosperity.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered July 3, 2021 as the keynote and induction address at PICPA's national conference, this speech by CJP -- who opens by humorously questioning why Dolly Miguel invited 'not a CPA, not even a commerce or business administration graduate' to be their inducting officer -- makes the case that CPAs, CFOs and CEOs are directly relevant to the philosophy of liberty and prosperity under the rule of law through the four TATS values: Transparency, Accountability, Truth and Sustainability. He first establishes the relationship with incoming PICPA President Dolly Miguel through their shared PLDT, MPIC, Meralco and GMA7 experience -- she as SGV partner-in-charge of external audits, he as Audit Committee chairman -- noting the multi-jurisdictional complexity of auditing PLDT (NYSE-listed, HK-listed parent, Philippine regulations) and Dolly's consistent performance under intense grilling. His L&P thesis is anchored in MLK ('If a man does not have a job or an income, he has neither life nor liberty nor the possibility for the pursuit of happiness') -- quoted not for his nationality but because 'truth is eternal and limitless; truth is not bound by sovereignty, or territory, or ideology.' He proves the entrepreneurship-prosperity link through three natural experiments: the US (pioneers unleashing Edison, Ford, Gates, Jobs, Bezos, contained by good governance); China (Deng Xiaoping's One-Country-Two-Systems unlocking Jack Ma and others); and the Korea comparison (South's private-initiative prosperity vs. North's poverty from tight grip on freedom). He then argues that different nations can sequence liberty and prosperity differently but must eventually achieve both in equal measure. TATS values, he concludes, make accountants 'images and collaborators of Martin Luther King, of Confucius and his fisherman, of Thomas Edison, of J.P. Morgan, of Franklin Delano Roosevelt, of Steve Jobs and even of Deng Xiaoping and Jack Ma.' He closes with FLP's three first-decade programs (20 law scholarships, dissertation contests, 17 professorial chairs) and announces the second-decade ESMEL expansion -- including a proposed AIM MBA major in Legal Management welcomed by AIM President Jikyeong Kang.
